endorsements.quote: These programs should be conducted in diverse settings to ensure the generalizability of results and include rigorous evaluation protocols to assess the impact on patient outcomes, provider workload, and healthcare costs.
Crucially, AI chatbots cannot replace human clinical judgment.
Additionally, they need to understand when to override or supplement AI recommendations with clinical judgment.

Ensuring informed consent and patient autonomy is crucial, including transparency about the use of AI systems, clear explanations of data usage and protection, and the right to refuse AI-assisted care without compromising access to traditional treatment.

Therefore, ongoing patient education about the capabilities and limitations of AI chatbots is vital, ensuring that individuals are empowered to seek human support when necessary.

The use of AI chatbots should enhance rather than replace the human-to-human therapeutic relationship, and patients should have access to human providers for aspects of care that require genuine empathy and emotional support.
Efforts must be made to ensure that the data used to train AI chatbots is diverse and representative of the population they will serve.
Regular audits of AI chatbot performance should be implemented to identify and address any emerging biases or disparities in care recommendations.

Collaboration between technology developers and medical professionals plays a key role in creating AI chatbots that meet the practical needs of primary care settings, involving joint development of clinical algorithms, refinement based on clinical feedback, and co-designing user interfaces to align with clinical workflows.

unlisted_practices: Establish clear protocols for when AI chatbots escalate to human providers.
Conduct small-scale pilot testing of AI chatbots and gather feedback from providers and patients before wider deployment.
Engage key stakeholders, including primary care providers, mental health specialists, IT staff, and patient representatives, in planning and implementing AI chatbots.
Train healthcare providers on AI chatbot capabilities, limitations, and interpreting AI recommendations, with ongoing updates as the system evolves.
Establish continuous feedback loops involving patients and clinicians to refine AI tools.
Select AI chatbots based on practice needs, integration capabilities, user interface, and evidence of effectiveness.
